infra_maya: Heads-up — scheduling a short "quiet hour" maintenance for network sanity checks + GPU pool deep-clean. Sat 2026-03-28 02:30-04:30 UTC (shifted 30m). Target: pool-quiet-03 (us-west2). Action: rolling cordon -> drain -> reboot -> uncordon for up to 8 nodes. Low-traffic window but please flag any tenant / dedicated contract blockers now.

oncall_bot: [AUTO] Maintenance event created: 7987654321 — quiet-hour network sanity & GPU cordon (02:30-04:30 UTC) — notified infra, oncall, support.

devops_jamal: Quick Q — what capacity are we backfilling from? If we drain 8 nodes that's ~32 GPUs (T4 equiv). Can we route traffic to burst pool or do reserved fallbacks? Need to check Dedicated customers.

sre_ava: Recommend canary on 1 node first, then 2, then rest in cohorts of 2. Will run a health probe after each uncordon: check active sessions, kv-cache hitrate, tail latencies. Example commands below.

platform_tom: Routing note — US-WEST2 multi-az fallback is fine, but APAC customers hit peak around 03:00 UTC; keep fallbacks limited. If we spin up extra instances for backfill that will trigger burst pricing in that region. Consider max 20% burst.

infra_maya: Ok — plan updated: start 02:30 UTC, cohorts of 2 nodes, max 8 nodes total. We'll notify enterprise accounts (two flagged customers) and ask them to pause heavy jobs. Jamal, can you own the canary and confirm Dedicated fallbacks?

devops_jamal: I got it. Canary run on the first node, I'll validate model-serving sessions and GPU process settle time. If we need reserved fallback, estimate ~ $120/hr extra for the backup pool (based on last month usage) — rough calc: 8 GPUs * $15/hr. If we use spot backfills it's cheaper but riskier.

sre_ava: Drain script I'm going to use (iterative, cohorts of 2):
```
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=pool-quiet-03 -o name | head -n 2); do
  kubectl cordon $n
  kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
  ssh $n 'sudo reboot' || echo "reboot failed $n"
  sleep 90
  kubectl uncordon $n
  # run health probes:
  curl -sS http://infra-health/api/pool-quiet-03/health | jq .
  sleep 30
done
```
Also will watch these metrics: prod.request.lat50, prod.request.lat99, kv_cache/hit_rate, gpu_utilization. If lat99 > 600ms for +2 probes we stop.

infra_maya: After uncordon please run KV cache warm seed (50k tokens) for top 3 prefixes to avoid cold-start regen. Command: `./tools/kv-warm --pool pool-quiet-03 --prefixes top-prompts.txt --tokens 50000`

sre_ava: Will run warm seed after each cohort. Also I'll post a quick grep to tail logs for stuck sessions: `kubectl logs -l app=model-server --since=1m | grep -E "stall|retry|OOM"`

devops_jamal: :thumbsup: I'll run the canary and post results at +15m from start. If anything odd I'll pause and we can revert uncordon -> manual rollback.

infra_maya: Thanks — support and account managers notified. I'll post a public comm in #general 15m before start and update ops-runbook: https://redwood.internal/docs/ops/quiet-hour-clean (ops-runbook has checklist + rollback steps).

oncall_bot: [AUTO] Maintenance 7987654321 confirmed: 02:30-04:30 UTC. Reminders scheduled 15m and 5m before start.

platform_tom: One more note — please ensure model-variant fallback policy is enabled for the cohort (route to smaller-quantized variant if latency spikes). I pushed a policy change to staging earlier, can apply during window.

infra_maya: Got it. Applying fallback policy during canary. If all good we'll proceed with the rest. I'll update this thread with the canary result.

devops_jamal: Canary done at +12m: node rebooted clean, kv-cache warm seed ran, prod.lat50 unchanged, prod.lat99 +10ms, kv hitrate +3%. Proceeding with cohort 2.

infra_maya: Excellent — proceeding. I'll keep monitoring and post a quick postmortem note after completion.
